source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Exact source records mapped to established public labels; mapping is recorded for every verse and verified against source KJV annotations. Daniel, Hosea, Joel, Jonah, Micah, and Nahum have chapter-boundary differences.

key_decisions.decision: Keeps the repeated lawsuit imperative and bodily imagery rather than sanitizing the accusation.
Preserves all threatened violence as the speaker's words, including killing rather than merely hardship.
Maintains the compassion motif and the explicit extension of judgment to children.
Keeps her reported rationale and the paired provisions that the response will reclaim.
Preserves the source's direct-address to third-person shift rather than smoothing it invisibly.
Retains the parallel failed pursuit and her pragmatic stated motive.
Keeps the emphatic giver and shift to plural they in the use of gold.
Links the possessive reversal to the earlier provision list and preserves nakedness.
Retains public humiliation and the hand image without euphemism.
Preserves the full calendar list, including Sabbaths rather than general holidays.
Keeps wages as part of the sexual-economic metaphor and the agricultural devastation.
Retains plural Baals and puts the emphatic forgotten speaker at the close.
Uses respond for anah, with sing possible in the note; keeps Achor and the exodus comparison.
Retains Baal to make the title/name wordplay teachable rather than silently using only master.
Maintains the return to third-person and the repeated names motif.
Keeps the nonhuman covenant partners and the unusual breaking of war itself.
Preserves feminine sowing then masculine response and the names' reversal rather than flattening pronouns.
